Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the 2024 Manifesto

This manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and declining public services, proposing significant investment and policy changes across multiple sectors.

## Healthcare and Social Care
The document proposes substantial NHS investment (£28bn annually by 2030) to reduce waiting lists, guarantee GP access, restore NHS dentistry, and boost staff pay. It advocates keeping healthcare publicly owned and opposes privatisation. For social care, it proposes free personal care, improved pay for carers, and £20bn annual investment.

## Housing
The manifesto calls for 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, introducing rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A major retrofit programme (£29bn over five years) would insulate homes to reduce energy costs and emissions.

## Energy and Climate
The document proposes transitioning to renewable energy, with wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030. It calls for ending new fossil fuel extraction, introducing a carbon tax, and bringing energy companies into public ownership. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy and Work
Proposals include £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways and water companies into public ownership, and establishing regional mutual banks. Worker protections would be strengthened through repealing anti-union legislation, introducing a £15 minimum wage, and pursuing 10:1 maximum pay ratios.

## Welfare and Taxation
The manifesto proposes increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, and ending the five-week benefit wait. Funding would come from wealth taxes on assets above £10m, reformed capital gains tax, and aligned investment income taxation.

## Environment and Nature
A Rights of Nature Act would give legal personhood to nature. The document proposes protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, bringing water companies into public ownership, and introducing a Right to Roam Act.

## Education
Proposals include £8bn school investment, free school meals, abolishing tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and moving academies under local authority control.

## Transport
The manifesto advocates public ownership of railways, £10bn annual public transport subsidies, free bus travel for under-18s, and £2.5bn annually for cycling and walking infrastructure. It proposes ending petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027.

## Democracy and Rights
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post voting, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and defending human rights legislation.

## Immigration
The document calls for ending the hostile environment, creating safe asylum routes, and abolishing minimum income requirements for family visas.

## International Affairs
The manifesto supports an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, recognising Palestine, ending arms exports to Israel, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI, and working toward EU membership. It advocates signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while acknowledging NATO's defensive role.

## Funding
The proposals would be funded through wealth and carbon taxes (estimated £50-70bn annually), business tax reforms, and borrowing for capital investment.
